items.name_html: a child is a full instance, not a subflow
items.body_html: the child is created by the ordinary CREATE_INSTANCE with its own L0f resolution, runtime_context, record, and LC1–LC4 lifecycle. L4 adds linkage + an event, not a new embedded execution model

items.name_html: idempotent spawn (child_key) — on the ACTIVE link
items.body_html: the same (parent instance, child step, child_key) yields at most one ACTIVE link (status spawning | active): a crash-replay re-entry reuses it and never double-spawns. A terminal link (a finished / failed / cancelled attempt) does not block — a recovery re-entry with the same child_key spawns a fresh attempt (new link_id). So retry is not a deadlock, and the idempotency is on the live link

the child's child_id lands in the parent link via a CHILD_SPAWNED kernel event (the RUNTIME_CONTEXT_READY analog), CAS'd + transcript-backed (spawning ⇒ active) — never an inline shorthand that could be lost. A lost CHILD_SPAWNED self-heals on the first CHILD_LIFECYCLE (the link binds the id then); the crash window (link durably spawning) is reconciled at L9

items.name_html: the parent owns the link; the child carries the back-ref
items.body_html: the canonical ChildWorkflowLink lives in the parent record; the child carries a parent_ref. (v1 had only a child id in plan metadata — no reverse link, so no reconciliation)

items.name_html: CHILD_LIFECYCLE is transition-based; the anchor is terminal
items.body_html: the event is produced by a child's subscribable lifecycle transition commit; the mechanism is general, but the MVP anchor subscribes only terminal transitions (done | failed | cancelled). Intermediate subscription (e.g. ready_for_human_approval) is a valid extension on the same channel

items.name_html: routing is fail-closed on the subscription
items.body_html: the parent resumes only on a lifecycle in its wait_for, on the matching link, while parked — else Rejected. The kernel knows no lifecycle meanings; wait_for keys route via the shared arrive()

the parent's round (a delivered-task cycle) and the child's round (the child's own loop) measure different things but use the same kernel mechanics — they are two independent instances, neither reads the other's round

items.name_html: a spawn that cannot start is a failed attempt
items.body_html: a static / typo'd template_ref is caught at load (child_template_ref_unresolved); a child CREATE_INSTANCE rejected past load (a dynamic binding / input invalid) emits CHILD_SPAWN_FAILED (the LC2 initiation-failure analog) → the parent's failed route (present by load — validate_child_steps requires a route for every terminal disposition), link terminal-failed. A transient spawn-dispatch crash (no event) leaves the link durably spawning → L9 re-drive (idempotent by request_id) — never a silent forever-wait
